title: Urabrask Defies the Machine Orthodoxy
summary: The furnace praetor shelters Mirrans and joins opposition to Norn's enforced conformity.
narrative: Urabrask's tolerance of Mirran refugees distinguished his furnaces from Norn's rigid Machine Orthodoxy.
His rebellion drew together enemies of Norn whose goals were not identical, including other Phyrexians.
His brutal punishment illustrated the internal violence concealed by Norn's promise of universal unity.

Urabrask's furnace layer offered an instructive contrast with Elesh Norn's Machine Orthodoxy. His relative tolerance of Mirran survivors did not mean he opposed all Phyrexian forms of transformation or shared the Mirrans' convictions. It established that the praetors did not interpret loyalty, freedom, and compleation in identical ways.

His opposition mattered strategically because Norn presented New Phyrexia as a unified civilization. Dissent within its own leadership made that image incomplete. Rebels who wished to remove Norn could cooperate against a common ruler while disagreeing profoundly about what should replace her system.

The punishment of Urabrask therefore belongs to the internal history of Phyrexia as well as the invasion of other planes. It shows how the campaign for universal incorporation also required force against inhabitants of New Phyrexia who refused to accept Norn's preferred version of perfection.
